descriptionChirho: Hifil causative sense: an agent actively separates or divides persons, groups, or things from one another, including the act of setting apart or distinguishing between categories.

Nifal reflexive/reciprocal sense: two or more parties part ways, separate from each other, or go their separate directions, whether voluntarily or by circumstance; includes imperatives and infinitives of mutual separation.

Nifal sense of physical branching or splitting, as when a river divides into separate streams or channels (Gen 2:10); focuses on geographic or structural division rather than interpersonal separation.
Qal passive and Pual sense describing a state of being spread apart or dispersed in space, used of things or limbs that are extended or scattered in various directions.
Hitpael and Nifal participial sense of being scattered or dispersed as a group, emphasizing the resultant state of wide dispersion of people or animals across an area.

Hitpael sense of coming apart or being pulled asunder, as bones becoming dislocated from their joints (Ps 22:14), or of things that can or cannot be pulled apart; focuses on physical dislocation rather than interpersonal or geographic separation.
Piel sense of going apart or withdrawing on one's own initiative, emphasizing individual voluntary departure from a group to be alone or to act independently.
